cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the clarity is starting to be yours.
cells.ask: Name one clear thing you notice about what you're tending, out loud, without adding what it means yet — just the thing itself.
cells.core:
You're noticing something come clear about what you're tending, and you're not rushing to shape it. The first cut is here before there's anything specific to do with it. That's the good version: attention before agenda. You catch the small shift in what's growing and you let it be small.

The bend shows up in the hand that tends. The clarity is real, but deciding what happens next can start before you've finished taking in what's in front of you. Try letting one observation sit unnamed for a day. What you're tending doesn't need the label to keep growing, and you don't need to know what it means to be the one who saw it.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what's growing without deciding what it means.
cells.verb: Seeing the first clear thing before it has a name
cells.place: Where something small is being tended and not yet forced

cells.tense: You are ahead of what's growing, writing the outcome before it has arrived.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're tending and do nothing to it today except look at it. No adjustment, no next step — one full day of just looking.
cells.core:
You're seeing a future version of what this could become — and you're already there, tending it, correcting it, making sure it arrives right. The care has turned into management. The thing you're growing hasn't asked for the outcome you're holding for it.

Clear seeing was supposed to cut through confusion, not rush past the present. When you're ahead of it, you miss what's actually happening now. The hurry takes from you the thing you're trying to protect. Pure presence is the way back: open, available, beginner's mind. Let one thing be un-steered today. It will not collapse without your hand on it, and you might see it for the first time.

cells.tense: You are still caring for something without seeing it clearly anymore.
cells.ask: Choose one thing you're tending and look at it for five minutes without fixing anything. Then say one true sentence about what you see — to yourself is enough.
cells.core:
There's something you're caring for, and you're doing it without the clear sight. You are present for the tasks — the feeding, the checking, the getting through — but the clarity dropped out and didn't fully come back. The caring is real. Sight isn't in it.

Running on empty, no direction shows in how you care now. Staying busy with what's growing is not the same as seeing it. The way back is not to push feeling into the caring; it's to choose one direction and look through it at what's here. Not compulsion, just a clear line from where you stand to what you're growing. That line is still available.

cells.tense: You are already seeing it clearly and calling that just part of the job.
cells.ask: Say it in your own voice: that was already seen. About one thing you've treated as obvious. Once, out loud or on paper.
cells.core:
You are already seeing what's growing — the shift, the early sign, the thing that hasn't fully arrived. You catch it before anyone names it, and you adjust quietly so it can keep going. You'd call that just paying attention.

The catching is running. The owning of it isn't. You keep it as a background function instead of something you're doing. But you're the one who spots it. That spotting has been steering the whole thing, and you've given it no name of your own. What's arriving now doesn't need you to be more awake; it needs you to know that the awake one is you.
cells.sheetLine: You're already the one seeing it. Start saying so.
